chunks: As for what Ibn Rabah narrated from Sama'ah, from al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning...
His, Exalted is He, saying: “and that you complete the number.”

So this report is like what has preceded, in that it is a solitary report that does not establish knowledge nor practice. The discussion regarding it is like the discussion regarding that one: it is not permissible to object by means of it to the outward meaning of the Qur'an and the mutawatir reports.

And even if it were sound, there would be nothing in it contrary to what we have said regarding the obligation of acting upon the crescents. That is because ruling that the count be completed for fasting as thirty days does not prevent the completion of what is in the month, if it is deficient, from being the fasting of twenty-nine days, since what is meant by completing the count is the days that are the days of the month in whatever state it may be.
And there is no disagreement that a month which is twenty-nine days is truly a month, not metaphorically.

And we do not deny that what is obligatory upon us, when there is obscurity regarding the crescent of Shawwal, is that we complete the month as thirty days, and that this is also obligatory when there is knowledge of the month’s completeness.
And when the matter is as we have described it, reliance upon it in opposition to what is known from the Shari'ah falls away.

key_terms.إِكْمَالِ ٱلْعِدَّةِ: completion of the required count of days
key_terms.خَبَرٌ وَاحِدٌ: a solitary report that does not establish certainty on its own
key_terms.ظَاهِرِ ٱلْقُرْآنِ: the outward, apparent meaning of the Qur'an
key_terms.هِلَالِ شَوَّالٍ: the crescent of Shawwal marking the end of Ramadan
key_terms.ٱلْأَهِلَّةِ: the lunar crescents used to determine the beginning and end of the month
key_terms.ٱلْعِدَّةَ: the counted number of days to be completed in the context of fasting

ai.seo_question: Does the verse “and that you complete the number” mean Ramadan must always be thirty days?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the verse “and that you complete the number” in relation to fasting, arguing that a solitary report cannot override the apparent meaning of the Qur'an or mutawatir hadith. It explains that completing the count does not negate the validity of a lunar month being twenty-nine days, while affirming the obligation to complete thirty days when the Shawwal crescent is obscured.
